title: Multicultural Counseling
tagline: Every child arrives with a whole culture.
welcome: Competence across culture is not an add-on to counseling; it is counseling, done honestly. This course trains the humble, skilled cross-cultural counselor.
vignette: A counselor praises a ten-year-old for 'speaking up for herself,' and watches the child's grandmother stiffen. In that silence, two cultures meet. The counselor must learn to read the room in more than one language of meaning.
vignette_attr: A cross-generational moment, drawn from practice
description: A study of multicultural and social-justice competencies in counseling children and adolescents: cultural identity development, bias and microaggressions, culturally responsive assessment and intervention, working with immigrant and minority families, and advocacy.
questions: What do I not see about my own culture?
How does bias enter assessment and diagnosis?
How do I honor a family's worldview while protecting a child?
importance: Culture shapes every symptom, story, and goal
Bias in assessment produces real harm and misdiagnosis
Families trust counselors who respect their world
misconceptions: that being kind is the same as being competent across culture
that culture matters only for minority clients, when every client is cultural
figures: whose multicultural competencies redefined the field
whose identity development models map the journey
outcomes: You will map your own position and its blind spots.
You will catch bias in yourself and in systems, and repair it.
You will choose and interpret tools with cultural validity.
You will modify methods without diluting evidence.
Work effectively with immigrant and minority families
You will build alliance across language and tradition.
You will act beyond the room for justice and access.
modules: Identity models let you meet people where they are.
Bias is human; unchecked bias is malpractice.
Assessment must ask: in this culture, what is this?
Adaptation keeps evidence and respect together.
Immigrant children carry two worlds; we hold both.
tips: Seek feedback from people whose culture differs from yours
Learn one concrete norm before each new community
Treat every family as the expert on their own life
integration: Multicultural competence permeates every clinical course and your entire practice.
faith: Every culture bears part of the image of God; honoring culture is a form of honoring the child.
closing: May you cross every cultural bridge with humility, and may no child feel foreign in your presence.
